text: Carl Handellen Nov 06, 2026 Share “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.” - Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and hundreds of other “researchers”, 2023.¹ Really? Pandemics? Nuclear war?! The worst possible things that could ever happen to the human race? Really?! “If someone builds a too-powerful AI, under present conditions, I expect that every single member of the human species and all biological life on Earth dies shortly thereafter.” - Eliezer Yudkowsky, Senior Research Fellow MIRI, 2023.² For fuck’s sake. This is so frightening. Since November 2022, life has certainly changed. AI has, and will continue to, permeate our everyday interactions with technology. Just recently I was forced to use AI to order at Wendy’s, yesterday I was trying to open a Facebook ticket and was only able to talk to an awful internal AI designed to frustrate you to the point where you just give up. So, AI is definitely here, I don’t need to make that argument, and with a lot of exceptions aside, it can actually be quite powerful. As a software engineer, I don’t write code anymore. Yeah. The keystone of my profession is basically over. But with all the new capabilities of AI, is it going to take over the world? Is it going to eradicate BIOLOGICAL LIFE from the planet? Almost certainly not. And those that push this narrative should be held responsible for their egregiously wrong predictions that end up being simply noise. I’m sure this will be pushed aside as simply “AI-denialism” or “AI skeptic slop” or even “naive optimism” and the “intellectuals” who see themselves as the holders of AI Safety knowledge will simply pass on by without reevaluating their strongly held opinions, strongly held. But this isn’t for them, it’s for all the other people being scared into their bunkers and hoarding their groceries in fear of a mysterious super intelligence that we created, and continue to create by the very people who claim it will kill us all. Let’s break down their claim that AI will kill all humans. That’s not an exaggeration. That’s what employees of Anthropic, the people who are working on the most advanced AI on the planet, are saying. In a post from X, Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science Lead at Anthropic, said: “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!”. Exclamation point. Wow. “Earnestly”. Damn. He goes on to predict it is greater than 10% within the next decade.³ He has some proof right? Wait there is a paper or something you guys are writing internally who believe this right? You have a thesis on how this would happen right? There is a timeline of potential events right? No. There is none of that. That’s it. How about the now famous, infamous?, Jacob Coxon. Jacob had a short career at Anthropic as a pretraining researcher. He was at OpenAI before that. When he resigned from Anthropic he had a premeditated press event launched where he said on X, “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade”. There is that word “earnestly” again.⁴ Again, zero proof. There is no “and I believe this because of this data that will also convince you”. There is no “these are the key events and discoveries that are leading me to this conclusion”. Alright well two random employees at Anthropic certainly don’t speak for the entire field of AI Safety and certainly don’t speak for Anthropic. Let’s see what Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, has to say. “There is a 25% chance that things go really, really badly, with a 75% chance things go “really, really well”.⁵ Zero proof? Really? You’re just going to throw that out there and walk away huh? No thesis on how it will happen. No modeling. Nothing. Instead, we must appeal to the authority of the people who are building the models to tell us the very thing they are building has a high chance of destroying all mankind, potentially all biological life. And because they are the authority, we should listen not only to their predictions but also their solutions as well. This is fucking exhausting. From what I can stitch together through debates and conversations and looking over the Effective Altruism message board, this 10% or 25% chance of all of mankind being exterminated, is based on the idea that we will achieve “super intelligence” where the models themselves will be far more intelligent than humans and capable of recursively getting more intelligent indefinitely. These models would be able to outsmart any mere human and would see humans as an obstacle to their survival and exterminate us. So not only do we have to achieve “super intelligence” and not hit any bottlenecks along the way, this super intelligence has to come to the conclusion that we are somehow in its way. And then the super intelligence has to be able to come up with some way to destroy all of mankind undetected and without natural access to the physical environment. And that’s a 25% chance? You know what a 100% chance is? If you purposefully slow down or halt AI development the US economy, and thus the world economy, will move very quickly into recession territory where millions and millions of people won’t be able to pay their bills and certainly will suffer. We saw it yesterday with just the threat of AI regulation by US politicians after the midterms. The NASDAQ fell into correction territory and had its biggest single day loss of all time. What’s the motives of the researchers and the CEOs of the major AI firms to be peddling this nonsense? I can only speculate. Is it that the young researchers come from a similar “doomer” world view and are enamored with the idea of “effective altruism”? Maybe. Is it that Dario, the CEO of Anthropic, along with Sam Altman the CEO of OpenAI, are looking to solidify their position as an effective monopoly by introducing strict regulation and banning their biggest competition, Open Source models?
